# `company.opening_drafts`

Guided opening balances: what an owner typed toward an opening, planned, posted and tied out through the cutover engine as one reversible batch. Never deleted.

Database: `company`.

| Column | SQL type | Nullable | Default | Key | Indexes | References | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | VARCHAR(26) | no | — | primary key 1 | — | — | Stable ULID of the draft. |
| `label` | VARCHAR(200) | no | — | — | — | — | What the draft is, as a person reads it. |
| `as_of` | VARCHAR(10) | no | — | — | — | — | The cutover date: balances are as of the end of this day. |
| `state` | VARCHAR(16) | no | — | — | — | — | draft, planned (a plan was read), applying (posting; the same command continues it), applied, rolled_back (a refusal undid what it posted), failed (that undo was refused; reverse it once cleared), reversed (undone as one unit) or discarded. |
| `files` | TEXT | no | — | — | — | — | JSON: each step (balances, open_invoices, unpaid_bills, stock) and its rows, as pasted text or an attachment id, with the date order when given. |
| `given` | TEXT | no | — | — | — | — | JSON: the totals the owner gave to check against (receivables, payables, stock), as amounts; a total left out is taken from the rows. |
| `make_items` | TEXT | no | — | — | — | — | JSON list of stock items a person confirmed may be made as new inventory parts. |
| `clearing_account` | VARCHAR(200) | yes | — | — | — | — | The clearing account named; null for Cutover Clearing. |
| `batch_id` | VARCHAR(26) | yes | — | — | — | batches.id | The batch the opening posted in; null until it is applied. |
| `summary` | TEXT | yes | — | — | — | — | JSON of the last plan or apply: ready, counts, checks and blocking lines; null before. |
| `version` | INTEGER | no | — | — | — | — | Optimistic-concurrency version of the draft. |
| `created_at` | VARCHAR(32) | no | — | — | ix_opening_drafts_created | — | UTC time it was made. |
| `created_by` | VARCHAR(26) | no | — | — | — | — | Principal that made it. |
| `updated_at` | VARCHAR(32) | no | — | — | — | — | UTC time of the last change. |
| `applied_at` | VARCHAR(32) | yes | — | — | — | — | UTC time it was applied; null before. |
